subproblems.title: Dual coefficient norm on n-vectors: continuous, nonnegative, dominating, and attained on the unit covector ball
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ there is a function N from n-vectors to ℝ with the following properties. Here n-vectors are the continuous linear functionals ζ on the space Λⁿ(ℝ^P) of n-covectors (MultiVector P n, with the operator-norm topology), and |α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I strictly increasing} α(e_{I(1)},…,e_{I(n)})²)^{1/2} with (e_i) the standard basis of ℝ^P. (i) N is continuous; (ii) N(ζ) ≥ 0 for every ζ; (iii) |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)·|α| for every n-vector ζ and every n-covector α; (iv) for every n-vector ζ there is an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(β) = N(ζ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), ∃ N : MultiVector P n → ℝ, Continuous N ∧ (∀ ζ : MultiVector P n, 0 ≤ N ζ) ∧ (∀ (ζ : MultiVector P n) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ζ α| ≤ N ζ * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∀ ζ : MultiVector P n, ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ζ β = N ζ)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (dual norm), with the omitted linear algebra filled in.

Notation:
- V := Λⁿ(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n, with its operator norm ‖·‖.
- e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P (EuclideanSpace.basisFun).
- For J : Fin n → Fin P, e_J := (e_{J(1)}, …, e_{J(n)}).
- |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{J strictly increasing} α(e_J)²).

An n-vector ζ is a continuous linear functional on V; MultiVector P n carries the operator norm.

1. Coordinate bound. Let I be strictly increasing. Then α(e_I)² is one of the nonnegative summands defining |α|². Hence α(e_I)² ≤ Σ_J [J strictly increasing] α(e_J)² (Finset.single_le_sum), and |α(e_I)| = √(α(e_I)²) ≤ |α| (Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs, Real.sqrt_le_sqrt).

2. Definiteness: if α(e_I) = 0 for every strictly increasing I, then α = 0.
(a) First, α(e_J) = 0 for every J : Fin n → Fin P.
- If J is not injective, then the tuple e_J is not injective (e is injective), so α(e_J) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective).
- If J is injective, let σ := Tuple.sort J. This is a permutation of Fin n with J∘σ monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort). J∘σ is injective, hence strictly monotone (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective), so α(e_{J∘σ}) = 0 by hypothesis. Since e_{J∘σ} = e_J∘σ, alternation gives 0 = α(e_J∘σ) = sign(σ)·α(e_J) (AlternatingMap.map_perm). As sign(σ) = ±1 is invertible, α(e_J) = 0 (smul_eq_zero_iff_eq).
(b) Now take any v = (v_1, …, v_n) and expand v_i = Σ_j v_i(j)·e_j (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr, EuclideanSpace.basisFun_repr). Multilinearity gives α(v) = Σ_{r : Fin n → Fin P} α((v_i(r(i))·e_{r(i)})_i) = Σ_r (Π_i v_i(r(i)))·α(e_r) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_sum, map_smul_univ). Every α(e_r) = 0 by (a), so α = 0.

3. Properties of |·|.
(i) |·| is continuous on V: α ↦ α(e_I) is evaluation at a fixed tuple (continuous_eval_const), and squares, finite sums and √ are continuous.
(ii) |tα| = |t|·|α|: every summand gains the factor t², and √(t²S) = |t|√S (Finset.mul_sum, Real.sqrt_mul, Real.sqrt_sq_eq_abs).
(iii) |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
(iv) If |α| = 0 then α = 0: by step 1, |α(e_I)| ≤ 0 for every strictly increasing I, so step 2 applies.

4. Finite dimension and norm comparison. Let L : V → ((Fin n → Fin P) → ℝ) be the linear map with (Lα)(I) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing and 0 otherwise.
- L is injective by step 2, so V is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective) and hence a proper metric space (FiniteDimensional.proper_real).
- L is antilipschitz: there is K > 0 with ‖α‖ ≤ K‖Lα‖ for all α (LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith with ker L = ⊥, applied to the points 0 and α).
- The target carries the sup norm, and each coordinate of Lα has absolute value at most |α| (step 1, or it is 0). So ‖Lα‖ ≤ |α| (pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg).
Therefore ‖α‖ ≤ K|α| for all α ∈ V.

5. Compact unit ball. B := {β ∈ V : |β| ≤ 1} is closed by step 3(i) and bounded because ‖β‖ ≤ K on B by step 4. As V is proper, B is compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded). Also 0 ∈ B (covectorEuclideanNorm_zero).

6. Definition of N. For an n-vector ζ, the set ζ(B) ⊆ ℝ is compact (continuous image) and nonempty. Define N(ζ) := sup ζ(B).
- N(ζ) ∈ ζ(B) (IsCompact.sSup_mem): there is β ∈ B, i.e. |β| ≤ 1, with ζ(β) = N(ζ). This is clause (iv).
- ζ(β′) ≤ N(ζ) for every β′ ∈ B (le_csSup; ζ(B) is bounded above by compactness).

7. Nonnegativity. 0 ∈ B and ζ(0) = 0, so N(ζ) ≥ 0. This is clause (ii).

8. Domination. Suppose |α| = 0. Then α = 0 by step 3(iv), and both sides of |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)|α| are 0. Otherwise let β := |α|⁻¹α. Then |β| = 1 by step 3(ii), so β ∈ B, and −β ∈ B by step 3(iii). Since α = |α|β, we get ζ(α) = |α|ζ(β) ≤ |α|N(ζ) and −ζ(α) = |α|ζ(−β) ≤ |α|N(ζ). Hence |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)|α|. This is clause (iii).

9. Continuity. For n-vectors ζ, ζ′ pick β ∈ B with ζ(β) = N(ζ) (step 6). Then N(ζ) = ζ′(β) + (ζ − ζ′)(β) ≤ N(ζ′) + ‖ζ − ζ′‖·‖β‖ ≤ N(ζ′) + K‖ζ − ζ′‖. This uses the operator-norm bound (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm) and ‖β‖ ≤ K from step 4. By symmetry N is K-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.of_le_add_mul), hence continuous. This is clause (i).

Steps 6–9 give all four clauses. ∎
proof_key_steps: Coordinate bound |α(e_I)| ≤ |α|. Definiteness: α vanishes if all strictly increasing coordinates vanish (sorting permutation, alternation, multilinear expansion).
The coordinate map L is injective, so covectors are finite-dimensional and ‖α‖ ≤ K|α|; the unit ball B = {|β| ≤ 1} is compact.
N(ζ) := sup ζ(B) is attained and nonnegative, and |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)|α| by rescaling α to |α|⁻¹α ∈ B.
N is K-Lipschitz for the operator norm, hence continuous.

subproblems.title: Positive lower n-density of a finite measure on a set forces finite Hⁿ-measure (Vitali 5r-covering)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P with μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, let A ⊆ ℝ^P be an arbitrary set and let η > 0. Suppose liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_n·rⁿ) ≥ η for every x ∈ A. Here B_r(x) is the open ball, ω_n = unitBallVolume n is the volume of the unit ball of ℝⁿ, and the quotient is computed in [0, ∞] with rⁿ entering through ENNReal.ofReal. Then Hⁿ(A) < ∞, where Hⁿ = μHE[n].
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (η : ℝ), 0 < η → μ univ < ∞ → (∀ x ∈ A, ENNReal.ofReal η ≤ liminf (fun r : ℝ => μ (ball x r) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0)) → μHE[n] A < ∞
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 5 (Vitali covering; a non-sharp constant suffices), stated for an arbitrary set A and filled in.

Notation: ω_n := unitBallVolume n = volume(B_1(0) ⊆ ℝⁿ); μH[n] is Mathlib's unnormalized Hausdorff measure; B_r(x) and B̄_r(x) are the open and closed balls; all quantities lie in [0, ∞].

1. Constants. 0 < ω_n < ∞, because B_1(0) is a nonempty bounded open subset of ℝⁿ and volume on Euclid n is an additive Haar measure (measure_ball_pos, measure_ball_lt_top). Put c := ofReal(η/2)·ω_n. Then 0 < c < ∞.

2. Arbitrarily small good radii. Let x ∈ A and δ > 0. As η > 0, ofReal(η/2) < ofReal(η) ≤ liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)). Hence the quotient exceeds ofReal(η/2) for all r in some set belonging to 𝓝[>]0 (Filter.eventually_lt_of_lt_liminf). Intersect with (0, δ) ∈ 𝓝[>]0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT); since 𝓝[>]0 is a proper filter, there is ρ ∈ (0, δ) with ofReal(η/2) < μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)). Then c·ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(η/2)·(ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) (ENNReal.mul_le_of_le_div and monotonicity).

3. Radii at scale k. For k ∈ ℕ let δ_k := 1/(k+1). By step 2 and choice there are functions r_k : ℝ^P → ℝ with, for all x ∈ A, 0 < r_k(x) < δ_k and c·ofReal(r_k(x)ⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_{r_k(x)}(x)).

4. Vitali subfamily. Apply the Vitali covering lemma (Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement_closedBall) with index set A, centers x ↦ x, radii r_k ≤ δ_k and τ = 5 > 3. It gives u_k ⊆ A such that the balls B̄_{r_k(b)}(b), b ∈ u_k, are pairwise disjoint, and every a ∈ A has some b ∈ u_k with B̄_{r_k(a)}(a) ⊆ B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b). Since a ∈ B̄_{r_k(a)}(a), A ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u_k} B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b). Each B̄_{r_k(b)}(b) contains the nonempty open ball B_{r_k(b)}(b), so it has nonempty interior. As ℝ^P is separable, u_k is countable (Set.PairwiseDisjoint.countable_of_nonempty_interior).

5. Radius sum. Countable additivity over the disjoint Borel balls (measure_biUnion) gives Σ_{b∈u_k} μ(B̄_{r_k(b)}(b)) = μ(⋃_{b∈u_k} B̄_{r_k(b)}(b)) ≤ μ(ℝ^P). With step 3, c·Σ_{b∈u_k} ofReal(r_k(b)ⁿ) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left). Multiplying by c⁻¹ (c ≠ 0, ∞) gives Σ_{b∈u_k} ofReal(r_k(b)ⁿ) ≤ c⁻¹μ(ℝ^P).

6. Diameters. For y, z ∈ B̄_{5r}(b), dist(y, z) ≤ dist(y, b) + dist(z, b) ≤ 10r. So diam B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b) ≤ ofReal(10r_k(b)) ≤ ofReal(10δ_k) (Metric.ediam_le_of_forall_dist_le). The map t ↦ tⁿ is monotone on [0, ∞] (ENNReal.rpow_le_rpow, exponent n ≥ 0), and ofReal(10r)ⁿ = 10ⁿ·ofReal(rⁿ) for r ≥ 0. Hence Σ_{b∈u_k} (diam B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b))ⁿ ≤ 10ⁿ·Σ_{b∈u_k} ofReal(r_k(b)ⁿ) ≤ 10ⁿ·c⁻¹·μ(ℝ^P) =: Λ. Λ < ∞ because μ(ℝ^P) < ∞ and c > 0.

7. Hausdorff bound. For each k, the countable family (B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b))_{b∈u_k} covers A, with diameters ≤ ofReal(10δ_k) → 0 as k → ∞. Apply Measure.hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum with exponent n, filter atTop on ℕ, and index types the countable subtypes u_k. It gives μH[n](A) ≤ liminf_k Σ_{b∈u_k} (diam B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b))ⁿ ≤ Λ, since every term is ≤ Λ (Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le').

8. Conclusion. By definition μHE[n] = s·μH[n], where s = addHaarScalarFactor(volume, μH[n]) is a finite nonnegative real (euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def). Hence μHE[n](A) ≤ s·Λ < ∞. ∎
proof_key_steps: From the liminf hypothesis, choose radii r_k(x) < 1/(k+1) with c·r_k(x)ⁿ ≤ μ(B̄_{r_k(x)}(x)), where c = (η/2)·ω_n ∈ (0, ∞).
Vitali 5r-lemma: a countable disjoint subfamily u_k ⊆ A with A ⊆ ⋃_{b∈u_k} B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b).
Σ diam(B̄_{5r_k(b)}(b))ⁿ ≤ 10ⁿ·Σ r_k(b)ⁿ ≤ 10ⁿ·c⁻¹·μ(ℝ^P) =: Λ < ∞, with diameters ≤ 10/(k+1).
hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_tsum gives μH[n](A) ≤ Λ; μHE[n] is a finite multiple of μH[n].

subproblems.title: The mass identity forces the representing n-vector field to attain 1 on the unit covector ball almost everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Γ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), and μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(ℝ^P) < ∞ and M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) = Γ.massOn ℝ^P = μ(ℝ^P). Let ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) be μ-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and all n-covectors α (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm), and suppose Γ(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every test n-form ω on ℝ^P. Then for μ-a.e. x there is an n-covector β with |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Γ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), μ univ < ∞ → Γ.massOn univ = μ univ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, Γ ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ∂μ) → ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∃ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm β ≤ 1 ∧ ξ x β = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2 (|ξ|* = 1 μ-a.e.), stated with an a.e. bound and only the total-mass identity. Uses the sibling dual_norm (Submission.cbr_ci_dr_multivector_dual_norm). |·| denotes covectorEuclideanNorm.

1. Dual norm. Take N from dual_norm, applied with P and n. N is continuous on n-vectors, N ≥ 0, |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)·|α| for all ζ and α, and for every ζ there is β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(β) = N(ζ). μ is a finite measure because μ(ℝ^P) < ∞.

2. The function f := N∘ξ. Put f(x) := N(ξ(x)). f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable as a continuous function of the a.e. strongly measurable ξ (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable). Take x with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α (μ-a.e. x), and choose β with |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = N(ξ(x)). Then f(x) = ξ(x)(β) ≤ |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1. Together with f ≥ 0 this gives 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 μ-a.e., so f is μ-integrable (Integrable.of_bound on a finite measure).

3. Admissible forms. Let ω be a test n-form on ℝ^P with |ω(y)| ≤ 1 for all y, and put g(x) := ξ(x)(ω(x)).
- g is μ-a.e. strongly measurable: ω is smooth, hence continuous, and g is the continuous evaluation map (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α) applied to the a.e. strongly measurable pair x ↦ (ξ(x), ω(x)).
- For every x, g(x) ≤ |g(x)| ≤ N(ξ(x))·|ω(x)| ≤ N(ξ(x)) = f(x), using N ≥ 0 and |ω(x)| ≤ 1.
- |g(x)| ≤ f(x) ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. x, so g is integrable.
Hence Γ(ω) = ∫ g dμ ≤ ∫ f dμ (integral_mono_ae).

4. Mass bound. M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) = Γ.massOn univ is the supremum of ofReal(Γ(ω)) over exactly the forms ω of step 3 (massAdmissibleOn univ n univ; the condition tsupport ω ⊆ ℝ^P is automatic). By step 3 each such value is ≤ ofReal(∫ f dμ). Therefore μ(ℝ^P) = Γ.massOn univ ≤ ofReal(∫ f dμ) (sSup_le). Since ∫ f dμ ≥ 0 and μ(ℝ^P) < ∞, (μ univ).toReal ≤ ∫ f dμ (ENNReal.toReal_le_of_le_ofReal).

5. f = 1 almost everywhere. The function 1 − f is μ-integrable and ≥ 0 μ-a.e. Its integral is ∫(1 − f) dμ = (μ univ).toReal − ∫ f dμ ≤ 0 (integral_sub, integral_const), and it is also ≥ 0. So ∫(1 − f) dμ = 0, hence 1 − f = 0 μ-a.e. (integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae). That is, N(ξ(x)) = 1 for μ-a.e. x.

6. Attainment. For each such x, the β from step 1 has |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = N(ξ(x)) = 1. This holds for μ-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take N from dual_norm; f := N∘ξ is a.e. strongly measurable with 0 ≤ f ≤ 1 μ-a.e., hence integrable.
For every admissible ω, Γ(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ ≤ ∫ f dμ, so μ(ℝ^P) = M_{ℝ^P}(Γ) ≤ ∫ f dμ.
∫(1 − f) dμ = 0 with 1 − f ≥ 0, so f = 1 μ-a.e.; attainment of N gives β with |β| ≤ 1 and ξ(x)(β) = 1.

subproblems.title: A strongly measurable, everywhere-bounded modification of an a.e. dual-norm-bounded n-vector field
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) a μ-a.e. strongly measurable field of n-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and all n-covectors α (|·| = covectorEuclideanNorm). Then there is a strongly measurable ζ : ℝ^P → Λ_n(ℝ^P) with |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every x ∈ ℝ^P and every n-covector α, and ζ = ξ μ-a.e.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n), AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → ∃ ζ : Euclid P → MultiVector P n, StronglyMeasurable ζ ∧ (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), |ζ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ ζ =ᵐ[μ] ξ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (Borel normalized field ζ := ξ₀/max(1, |ξ₀|*)), stated with an a.e. bound. Uses the sibling dual_norm (Submission.cbr_ci_dr_multivector_dual_norm). |·| denotes covectorEuclideanNorm.

1. Dual norm. Take N from dual_norm, applied with P and n. N is continuous, N ≥ 0, |ζ(α)| ≤ N(ζ)·|α| for all ζ and α, and every ζ has some β with |β| ≤ 1 and ζ(β) = N(ζ).

2. Bounded fields have N ≤ 1. If |ζ(α)| ≤ |α| for all α, take β as in step 1. Then N(ζ) = ζ(β) ≤ |ζ(β)| ≤ |β| ≤ 1.

3. Normalization map. Define F(ζ) := max(1, N(ζ))⁻¹·ζ on n-vectors. Since max(1, N(ζ)) ≥ 1 > 0, the map ζ ↦ max(1, N(ζ))⁻¹ is continuous (Continuous.max, Continuous.inv₀), and scalar multiplication is continuous, so F is continuous.

4. The modification. Let ξ₀ := AEStronglyMeasurable.mk ξ. It is strongly measurable and ξ = ξ₀ μ-a.e. (AEStronglyMeasurable.ae_eq_mk). Put ζ := F∘ξ₀. It is strongly measurable as a continuous function of a strongly measurable map (Continuous.comp_stronglyMeasurable).

5. Everywhere bound. Fix x and α, and let m := max(1, N(ξ₀(x))) > 0. Then |ζ(x)(α)| = m⁻¹·|ξ₀(x)(α)| ≤ m⁻¹·N(ξ₀(x))·|α| = (N(ξ₀(x))/m)·|α| ≤ |α|, because N(ξ₀(x)) ≤ m.

6. Agreement almost everywhere. For μ-a.e. x, both ξ₀(x) = ξ(x) and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all α hold. For such x, N(ξ₀(x)) = N(ξ(x)) ≤ 1 by step 2, so m = 1 and ζ(x) = 1⁻¹·ξ₀(x) = ξ(x). Hence ζ = ξ μ-a.e. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take N from dual_norm; a field bounded by |·| has N ≤ 1 (attainment).
F(ζ) := max(1, N(ζ))⁻¹·ζ is continuous; ζ := F∘ξ₀, where ξ₀ is the strongly measurable version of ξ, is strongly measurable.
|ζ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| everywhere since N(ξ₀(x)) ≤ max(1, N(ξ₀(x))); where ξ₀ = ξ and ξ is bounded, ζ = ξ₀ = ξ, so ζ = ξ μ-a.e.

subproblems.title: Radon–Nikodym density on a positive carrier: μ ≪ ν⌞M₀ with ν(M₀) < ∞ gives μ = (ν⌞M)·θ with θ > 0 on M ⊆ M₀
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let μ, ν be measures on ℝ^P with μ(ℝ^P) < ∞. Let M₀ ⊆ ℝ^P be a Borel set with ν(M₀) < ∞ and μ(ℝ^P ∖ M₀) = 0, and suppose μ(E) = 0 for every E ⊆ ℝ^P with ν(E) = 0. Then there are a Borel set M ⊆ M₀ and a Borel function θ : ℝ^P → ℝ with θ(x) > 0 for every x ∈ M such that μ = (ν⌞M).withDensity(x ↦ ofReal θ(x)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (M₀ : Set (Euclid P)), μ univ < ∞ → MeasurableSet M₀ → ν M₀ < ∞ → μ M₀ᶜ = 0 → (∀ E : Set (Euclid P), ν E = 0 → μ E = 0) → ∃ (M : Set (Euclid P)) (θ : Euclid P → ℝ), MeasurableSet M ∧ M ⊆ M₀ ∧ Measurable θ ∧ (∀ x ∈ M, 0 < θ x) ∧ μ = (ν.restrict M).withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (θ x))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 6–8 (Radon–Nikodym and the carrier), stated for a general measure ν in place of Hⁿ = μHE[n].

1. Finiteness. μ is finite. ν₀ := ν⌞M₀ (ν.restrict M₀) is finite, since ν₀(ℝ^P) = ν(M₀) < ∞ (isFiniteMeasure_restrict).

2. Absolute continuity μ ≪ ν₀. Let ν₀(E) = 0. Since M₀ is Borel, ν₀(E) = ν(E ∩ M₀) (Measure.restrict_apply'), so μ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 by hypothesis. Also μ(E ∩ M₀ᶜ) ≤ μ(M₀ᶜ) = 0. As E ⊆ (E ∩ M₀) ∪ (E ∩ M₀ᶜ), μ(E) = 0.

3. Lebesgue decomposition. μ and ν₀ are σ-finite, so μ = μ.singularPart ν₀ + ν₀.withDensity(μ.rnDeriv ν₀) (Measure.haveLebesgueDecomposition_add). By step 2, μ.singularPart ν₀ = 0 (Measure.singularPart_eq_zero_of_ac). Hence μ = ν₀.withDensity h, where h := μ.rnDeriv ν₀ : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] is Borel (Measure.measurable_rnDeriv) and h < ∞ ν₀-a.e. (Measure.rnDeriv_lt_top).

4. Carrier and density.
- M := M₀ ∩ {x : 0 < h(x)} ∩ {x : h(x) < ∞} is Borel (measurableSet_lt) and M ⊆ M₀.
- θ := 1_M·(h(·)).toReal is Borel (ENNReal.measurable_toReal, Measurable.indicator).
- For x ∈ M, θ(x) = h(x).toReal > 0, because 0 < h(x) < ∞ (ENNReal.toReal_pos).

5. h = 1_M·h ν₀-a.e. For ν₀-a.e. x, x ∈ M₀ (ae_restrict_mem) and h(x) < ∞. For such x: if h(x) = 0, both sides vanish; if h(x) > 0, then x ∈ M and both sides equal h(x).

6. Restricting to M. μ = ν₀.withDensity h = ν₀.withDensity(1_M·h) (withDensity_congr_ae, step 5) = (ν₀⌞M).withDensity h (withDensity_indicator, M Borel) = (ν⌞M).withDensity h. The last equality holds because ν₀⌞M = ν⌞(M ∩ M₀) = ν⌞M (Measure.restrict_restrict, M ⊆ M₀).

7. Replacing h by ofReal∘θ. For x ∈ M, ofReal(θ(x)) = ofReal(h(x).toReal) = h(x), since h(x) < ∞ (ENNReal.ofReal_toReal). As (ν⌞M)-a.e. x lies in M (ae_restrict_mem), h = ofReal∘θ (ν⌞M)-a.e. withDensity_congr_ae then gives μ = (ν⌞M).withDensity(x ↦ ofReal(θ(x))).

Together with step 4 (M Borel, M ⊆ M₀, θ Borel, θ > 0 on M), all clauses hold. ∎
proof_key_steps: ν₀ := ν⌞M₀ is finite and μ ≪ ν₀; the Lebesgue decomposition with zero singular part gives μ = ν₀.withDensity h with h = μ.rnDeriv ν₀ < ∞ ν₀-a.e.
M := M₀ ∩ {0 < h} ∩ {h < ∞} and θ := 1_M·h.toReal are Borel, with θ > 0 on M.
